generators.carrier: finite square matrices over a common finite-dimensional space
lists of P that are linear extensions

relations.statement: If x and y are incomparable (spacelike) and A_x A_y = A_y A_x, then the product of a list with x,y adjacent equals the product with them swapped.
relations.hypotheses: x and y incomparable; A_x and A_y commute

relations.statement: Any two linear extensions of a finite strict poset are connected by a finite sequence of swaps of adjacent incomparable elements.

lemmas.statement: For lists l1 l2 and incomparable x y with A_x A_y = A_y A_x, prod(l1 ++ [x,y] ++ l2) = prod(l1 ++ [y,x] ++ l2).
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem swap_lemma {n : Type} (A : n -> Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℚ) (l1 l2 : List n) (x y : n) (h : A x * A y = A y * A x) : (l1 ++ [x,y] ++ l2).map A |>.prod = (l1 ++ [y,x] ++ l2).map A |>.prod := by sorry

lemmas.statement: For a finite strict poset with matrices commuting on all incomparable pairs, the ordered product is the same for all linear extensions.

near_misses.claim: Two spacelike elements carrying anticommuting Paulis (e.g. X and Z) give the same product in both orders.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: XZ = -ZX, so the two orderings differ by a sign -1; commutation is required.

near_misses.claim: Swapping comparable elements preserves the product.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: A swap of comparable elements does not yield a linear extension, and the commutation hypothesis only covers incomparable pairs.
